A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExPLoRA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C. Renamed configurations and relocated experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ExPLoRA classification and segmentation experiments, parameter-unfreezing ablations, convergence results, and additional NAIP results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds GlobalWheat detection results, representation analyses, attention visualizations, and decoder-rank and backbone-size ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 restates v1's selective block and normalization unfreezing, Q/V LoRA updates, pretrained initialization, and continued self-supervised objective. The expanded head, decoder-rank, and storage descriptions provide implementation and configuration details without establishing a different ExPLoRA algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds GlobalWheat wheat-head detection in agricultural photographs, extending evaluation beyond the previous classification and segmentation tasks to bounding-box detection. All earlier dataset coverage remains, including EuroSAT, which moves to Appendix A.1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds substantial PEFT comparisons involving VPT variants, GVPT, SA2VP, and AdaLoRA, including SA2VP applied after ExPLoRA. GASSL and fully fine-tuned MAE disappear from that comparison, and the BOFT row changes its reported initialization from MAE to DinoV2. GASSL also disappears from the SpaceNet and RESISC-45 comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported DinoV2 pretraining learning rate from 0.001 to 0.002 and the RGB MAE rate from 0.00015 to 0.00045. New experiments introduce ViT-B/G configurations, decoder-rank controls, patch-level probes, and detection AP/AR evaluation. These reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun. EuroSAT's r64 label in v2 conflicts with its retained reference to the r32 model in Table 4.

E4.justification: V2 adds layer-wise PCA and position/class prediction probes in Section 6.3, attention-map case studies in Appendix A.2, decoder-rank sensitivity in A.4, and backbone-size analysis in A.5. Table 3 expands block-selection and VPT controls. The convergence comparison already existed as v1 Figure 3; v2 updates it and moves it to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance. V2's eigenvalue summaries and attention-score filtering describe feature analyses rather than uncertainty in the reported performance estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces ExPLoRA's fMoW-RGB linear-probing scores of 75.77/76.53 with 76.86/77.48, and several Table 3 ablation scores change. RESISC-45 linear-probing accuracy changes from 97.16 to 97.32. V2 adds detection, downstream comparison, and appendix ablation results; GlobalWheat reports 82.7 accuracy, 54.5 AP, and 59.2 AR. The main fMoW-RGB fine-tuning score remains 79.15. Revised pretraining settings prevent interpreting updated scores as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the final expression from W + BA to W0 + BA, fixing the weight-decomposition identity. Otherwise, source/target notation and equation ordering change without substantive changes to the formal assumptions or factorization; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient domain adaptation and strong downstream performance remain. V2 broadens claimed generalization to agricultural imagery and adds representation analysis as an explicit third contribution. It also revises the claimed linear-probing margin, including 7% to 7.5% in the abstract and approximately 8% in the introduction.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix A.2 add substantive explanations linking middle layers to local information and deeper layers to global semantics, using these observations to motivate block selection. Appendix A.4 argues that excessive decoder capacity can fail to improve encoder representations, while A.5 discusses diminishing returns from larger backbones. Earlier SpaceNet and iWildcam limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies shared-head initialization and dimensions, crop and masking settings, teacher EMA and temperatures, initial head freezing, and MAE loss options. It first discloses 32 gradient-accumulation steps and an effective DinoV2 batch size of 1024; this alone does not establish an increase over v1. It also adds Detectron2 implementation information, a GlobalWheat license reference, and a project-page code-access statement.

R1.justification: Related work expands locally to visual prompt tuning and its inference costs, adding VPT, GVPT, SA2VP, and E2VPT citations. V2 also adds GlobalWheat, Detectron2, and medical self-supervised learning references, while removing VideoMAE and point-cloud MAE citations. ExPLoRA's positioning as complementary to existing PEFT remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the problem setup, method explanations, and portions of the introduction and discussion. It introduces explicit pseudocode, shortens configuration names, adopts source/target terminology, and reorganizes training details by training phase. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds three representation-analysis plots, an attention-map grid, and new experimental tables. It expands Tables 1 and 3, combines SpaceNet and RESISC-45 into one table, relocates EuroSAT, and redraws and relocates the convergence plot. The document also adopts different title, heading, and running-header formatting.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited PEFT comparisons and largely heuristic explanation of block selection through Table 1, Section 6.3, and Appendices A.2, A.4, and A.5. Expanded implementation details make the work more reproducible, and detection results test broader applicability. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses, including conflicting EuroSAT rank labels and overstated PEFT margins: Table 1's 79.15 versus AdaLoRA's 78.87 supports only a 0.28-point advantage. The improvement rests on stronger scrutiny and documentation, not merely higher reported scores.
